newsitem.title: GERMANY: Microsoft Network shuts e-mail worldwide.
newsitem.headline: Microsoft Network shuts e-mail worldwide.

text.p: Microsoft Network, the U.S. software giant's online service, has shut down its worldwide electronic mail computers until Sunday, customer service officials at the company said on Thursday.
The network, with approximately 2.2 million subscribers, took the servers offline for unexpected maintenance work.
No prior announcement was made of the interruption in service, which could inconvenience many of the network's customers who rely on e-mail for business communications.

A message to customers on the Microsoft online service, the world's third largest, said the network experienced a partial outage of its e-mail service earlier this week that prompted it to accelerate an expansion of its e-mail capacity that had been planned for later this month.

Similar growing pains at rival America Online, the world's largest online provider with eight million members, led to a cyberspace blackout late last year that prompted a consumer outcry and culminated in lawsuits.
The rapid expansion of online services has sparked debate over whether they have an obligation to be as reliable as utilities such as telephone and electric service.

Microsoft said its e-mail expansion was planned due to growing membership, adding the current maintenance started late Wednesday Pacific time and would take 24 to 36 hours. Delivery of the e-mail backlog would take until Sunday, it said.
No mail will be lost, and the outage should not have an impact on the service as a whole, it said.

"We are doubling the number of our e-mail servers to serve you better. To accomplish this, we've temporarily taken our current mail servers off-line. As a result, members have been unable to send or receive mail since late Wednesday afternoon," the message to customers said.

"Service should be restored midday (Pacific time) Friday April 18. When the servers are back online, you should receive all e-mail that was sent to you during the upgrade. Delivery of delayed e-mail should be complete by Sunday April 20."
During the outage, customers will not able to contact member support on line, or cancel their accounts, it said.
The Microsoft Network's press spokeswoman for Germany was not immediately available for comment.
